text.title: user-flows.md Template — Worked Examples
text.summary: The five fields per flow, one complete worked flow in Markdown, the stripe-checkout illustration, the unsexy-edge list negatives are drawn from, and the skipped cases with what verifies them instead.

list.item: Actor — who is doing the flow (anonymous user, signed-in solo-tier user, admin).
Preconditions — what state the system must be in (account exists, payment method on file).
Happy path — numbered steps + expected result per step. The success criterion is in the final step.
Negative paths — at least one. Each: trigger (what causes the error), expected error UX (what the user sees, where).
Playwright spec path — relative path to the spec file that automates this flow.

example.code:
## Flow F-01: Signed-in user upgrades to solo tier
- Actor: signed-in free-tier user with verified email. - Preconditions: account exists; Stripe customer record exists; no active subscription. - Happy path: 1. Click "Upgrade" in nav → routed to /upgrade. 2. Select "Solo $19/mo" → Stripe Elements form appears. 3. Enter test card 4242 4242 4242 4242, submit. 4. Expect: 200 redirect to /account?upgraded=solo; success toast; tier=solo in /api/account. - Negative paths: - Card declined (test card 4000 0000 0000 0002): - Trigger: submit declined card. - Expected UX: inline error under card field "Your card was declined.", form stays editable, no charge created. - Network drop mid-submit: - Trigger: throttle network to offline after click submit. - Expected UX: spinner times out at 30s, toast "Connection lost. Try again." NO partial subscription. - Playwright spec: `faion-net-e2e/tests/upgrade.spec.ts`
example.note: Five fields, success criterion in step 4, two negatives each with trigger and expected UX, one spec file. This is the rendered form of the valid example in 02-output-contract.xml.
Feature: "stripe checkout page". user-flows.md documents the happy purchase flow + card-declined negative + 3DS-challenge negative + double-submit prevention. Each flow links to a Playwright spec.

section.title: Negative trumps positive (the unsexy-edge principle)
section.p: When there is time for only one extra test, write the negative one. Authentication failure, network drop, invalid input, race condition, double-submit — these are where regressions live. Happy paths get attention because they are easy to demo; negatives get attention only when something breaks at 3am.

list.item: Auth failure — wrong password, expired session, missing permission.
Network down — request times out, partial response, offline mode.
Invalid input — empty, too long, wrong type, hostile characters.
Boundary — first item, last item, page-size boundary, empty list.

section.title: SKIPPED cases and what verifies them instead

list.item: Backend API endpoint with no UI consumer in this feature → API tests only.
Background worker / job / cron → unit + integration tests.
Data migration → migration test + reversibility check.
